chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

It was said to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), 'What is the matter that the martyr is not tested in his grave?' So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The lightning above his head suffices as a test.'

key_terms.الْبَارِقَةِ: The lightning (referring to the wound or the flash of death)
key_terms.يُفْتَنُ: Is tested/tried (specifically referring to the trial in the grave)

ai.seo_question: Why are martyrs not tested in their graves according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this narration from al-Kafi highlights the unique spiritual status of the martyr, where the physical wounds of battle serve as expiation for minor sins, thereby sparing them the trial of the grave (fitnah al-qabr). The metaphor of 'lightning' (al-bariqah) signifies the intense, purifying impact of these wounds, a concept deeply rooted in the tradition of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding the immediate elevation of the martyr's soul.
